name: Rhode Island
surtax: From tax year 2027 (not 2026): 1% surtax on income above $1,000,000 (indexed), 2% in 2028, 3% from 2029 (H 7127 Sub A, FY2027 budget).
local: None (no municipal income tax in Rhode Island).
usInterest: Subtracted on RI Schedule M, line 1a: 'Income from obligations of the US government included in Federal AGI but exempt from state income taxes', reduced by related investment interest taken as a federal itemized deduction (2025 RI Schedule M).
sourceTitle: RI Division of Taxation ADV 2025-22, Inflation-adjusted amounts set for Tax Year 2026 (Nov 3, 2025) - Uniform tax rate schedule for Tax Year 2026
note: Re-read 2026-10-19 from Internet Archive captures (tax.ri.gov answers 403 to scripts): ADV 2025-22 (capture 2026-02-26) gives the Tax Year 2026 uniform schedule used by all filers: 3.75% to $82,050, 4.75% to $186,450, 5.99% above. The 2026 Summary of Legislative Changes (July 22, 2026; capture 2026-09-02) adds a 1% high-income surtax above $1 million only from tax year 2027 (2% in 2028, 3% from 2029): nothing new for 2026. 2026 standard deduction $11,200 single / $22,400 joint.

name: South Carolina
local: None (no local income tax in South Carolina).
usInterest: Subtracted from federal taxable income on SC1040 line 4m, 'Interest income from obligations of the US government' (2025 SC1040; the 2026 form is not yet published).
sourceTitle: S.C. General Assembly, H.4216 (Act No. 110 of 2026, ratified Mar 25 and signed Mar 30, 2026), amending S.C. Code 12-6-510(C) for taxable years beginning after 2025
note: Statutory table: $0-$30,000 at 1.99%; $30,000 or more at 5.21% times the amount minus $966 (this works as a marginal 5.21% above $30,000). The same schedule applies to every filing status. The statute says the brackets are 'indexed in accordance with Section 12-6-520', and SCDOR has not published an indexed 2026 figure, so $30,000 is taken as the 2026 value. The act also replaces the federal standard/itemized deduction with an SC Income Adjusted Deduction (SCIAD: $15,000 single, $30,000 MFJ, phased out by AGI). Contingent cuts to the top rate begin in TY2027. The SCDOR WH-1603F (Rev. 11/4/25) still shows the older 0%/3%/6% structure and is superseded.

name: South Dakota
sourceTitle: South Dakota Department of Revenue - Individuals: Taxes
note: The page states: 'South Dakota is one of seven states that does not impose a state income tax.'

name: Tennessee
local: None (the Hall tax was the only tax on interest and dividends; localities have no income tax).
usInterest: Not applicable. The Hall income tax on interest and dividends was repealed for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2021.
sourceTitle: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Hall Income Tax
note: Re-read 2026-10-19: tn.gov is unreachable from scripts; the Department of Revenue Hall Income Tax page was read from its Internet Archive capture of 2026: 'The Hall Income tax was repealed for tax periods that begin on January 1, 2021, or later.'

name: Texas
local: None (constitution bars any tax on individuals' net income).
sourceTitle: Texas Constitution, Art. 8, Sec. 24-a, Individual Income Tax Prohibited (added Nov. 5, 2019)
note: Sec. 24-a: 'The legislature may not impose a tax on the net incomes of individuals...'. Sec. 24-b also prohibits a capital gains tax.

name: Utah
local: None (no local income tax in Utah).
usInterest: Subtracted on TC-40A Part 2 using code 71 (U.S. Government obligations interest: Treasury bills, notes, E/EE/H/HH/I bonds; GNMA/FNMA not exempt), carried to TC-40 line 33. Source: https://incometax.utah.gov/subtractions/interest-us-obligations
sourceTitle: Utah S.B. 60 (2026 General Session) Income Tax Rate Amendments, Enrolled Copy - amends Utah Code 59-10-104 to 4.45%, retrospective to taxable years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026
note: Flat rate, down from 4.5% in 2025. The nonrefundable Utah taxpayer tax credit (based on deductions and exemptions) phases out as income rises, so the effective marginal rate inside the phase-out range is above 4.45%. tax.utah.gov is behind Cloudflare; the enacted bill on le.utah.gov was read instead.

name: Vermont
surtax: Minimum tax: when federal AGI exceeds $150,000, Vermont tax is the greater of the rate-schedule tax or 3% of federal AGI less interest from U.S. obligations.
local: None (Vermont local option taxes are sales, rooms and meals, not income).
usInterest: Subtracted on Schedule IN-112 Part I, line 7, 'Interest Income from U.S. Obligations' (2025). It is also excluded from the 3% AGI minimum-tax base.
sourceTitle: 2025 Form IN-111 Instructions - 2025 Vermont Tax Rate Schedules (Schedules X and Y-1)
note: 2026 individual rate schedules are not yet published: tax.vermont.gov/document/2026-vt-rate-schedules returns 'Page not Found', and the 2026 IN-114 contains no schedule. Only the 2026 withholding tables (GB-1210 / TaxTables-2026.pdf) exist; they use the same rates (3.35/6.60/7.60/8.75%) but wage thresholds, not taxable-income thresholds. Brackets are inflation-indexed each year, so the 2026 thresholds will be slightly higher.

name: Virginia
local: None (Virginia localities do not levy income taxes).
usInterest: Subtraction under Va. Code 58.1-322.02(1) for income derived from obligations of the United States (stocks, bonds, treasury bills, treasury notes), reported as a subtraction on Schedule ADJ of Form 760. The line number was not verified because the 2025 Schedule ADJ PDF could not be retrieved.
sourceTitle: Code of Virginia 58.1-320, Imposition of tax (as displayed 10/19/2026)
note: Statutory schedule unchanged since 1990 and not indexed. The same brackets apply to all filing statuses; married couples filing jointly do not get doubled brackets.

name: Washington
surtax: Capital gains excise tax (RCW 82.87): 7% on long-term capital gains above the standard deduction ($278,000 for 2025), plus 2.9% on the portion of capital gains above $1,000,000 from TY2025. It applies only to sales or exchanges of long-term capital assets, so interest income is not taxed. ESSB 6346 (Ch. 238, Laws of 2026) enacts a 9.90% tax on Washington taxable income above a $1,000,000 deduction, beginning January 1, 2028; its Sec. 306 requires deducting income from US obligations. It is likely to face court and ballot challenges.
usInterest: Not applicable for 2026. From 2028 under ESSB 6346, Sec. 306 ('Federal obligations') deducts income derived from obligations of the United States from Washington base income.
sourceTitle: Washington Department of Revenue - Capital gains tax
note: No personal income tax in 2026. The DOR page describes the 7% tax on the sale or exchange of long-term capital assets (stocks, bonds, etc.), which does not reach interest. Sources: RCW 82.87.040 at https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=82.87.040 (7% plus 2.90% above $1M) and the ESSB 6346 session law at https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/biennium/2025-26/Htm/Bills/Session%20Laws/Senate/6346-S.SL.htm (Sec. 201: tax beginning Jan 1, 2028 at 9.90%).

name: West Virginia
local: None on interest income (some municipal user/service fees on people who work in the city are not income taxes).
usInterest: Subtracted on IT-140 Schedule M, line 29: 'Interest or dividends received on United States or West Virginia obligations... included in federal adjusted gross income but exempt from state tax' (2025 IT-140 instructions).
sourceTitle: West Virginia Legislature, Enrolled Committee Substitute for Senate Bill 392 (2026 Regular Session) - new W. Va. Code 11-21-4j, Rate of tax for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2026
note: One table covers single, head of household and married filing jointly. Married filing separately uses half-width brackets (5,000/12,500/20,000/30,000). Signed March 31, 2026; effective June 12, 2026 and applies to TY2026. Further contingent cuts (11-21-4h) can start in TY2027 or later.

name: Wisconsin
local: None (no local income tax in Wisconsin).
usInterest: Subtracted on Schedule SB, line 2, 'United States government interest' (2025 Schedule SB).
sourceTitle: Wisconsin DOR, 2026 Form 1-ES instructions - 2026 Tax Rate Schedules for Full-Year Residents (Schedule A single/HOH, Schedule B married filing jointly)
note: Head of household uses the single schedule; married filing separately thresholds are 10,080/34,630/221,820. The sliding-scale standard deduction is significant (2026: up to $13,960 single, $25,840 MFJ, phased out by income).

name: Wyoming
sourceTitle: Wyoming Legislature, LSO Legal & Budget/Fiscal Divisions, 'Wyoming Tax Structure, Rates and Collections' (June 3, 2025)
note: Re-checked 2026-10-19. No Wyoming Department of Revenue page says it in words (revenue.wyo.gov and the Excise Tax Division pages have no income-tax text). The Wyoming Constitution published by the Secretary of State (amendments through November 18, 2024; https://sos.wyo.gov/Forms/Publications/WYConstitution.pdf) has no income tax and, in Art. 15 Sec. 18, requires any future income tax to credit sales, use and property taxes. The Legislative Service Office table (June 3, 2025) lists 'Individual Income Tax 0%' with no collections. No 2026 income tax law is known.

extraSources.title: Constitution of the State of Wyoming, Art. 15 Sec. 18 (Wyoming Secretary of State)
